reference_rules.rule: Every adjacent pair of grade levels has an overlapping salary band, allowing lateral transfers without mandatory pay cuts. Overlap grows with seniority: $10K at grades 1–3, $25K at grade 4–5, up to $50K at grades 9–10.
reference_rules.evidence: Grade 1 MAX=55000 > Grade 2 MIN=45000; Grade 2 MAX=70000 > Grade 3 MIN=60000; Grade 3 MAX=90000 > Grade 4 MIN=80000; Grade 4 MAX=120000 > Grade 5 MIN=95000; Grade 5 MAX=145000 > Grade 6 MIN=110000; Grade 6 MAX=170000 > Grade 7 MIN=130000; Grade 7 MAX=200000 > Grade 8 MIN=160000; Grade 8 MAX=250000 > Grade 9 MIN=200000; Grade 9 MAX=350000 > Grade 10 MIN=300000

reference_rules.rule: Salary band width grows with grade level, encoding that executive compensation is highly variable while entry-level pay is tightly constrained. Entry Level band is $20K wide; C-Suite band is $300K wide (15x wider).
The minimum salary at any grade is always at least 50% of its maximum, establishing a floor ratio that prevents excessively wide bands from being used to underpay within-band.
reference_rules.evidence: Grade 10: MIN=300000 / MAX=600000 = 50.0% (lowest ratio); Grade 1: MIN=35000 / MAX=55000 = 63.6% (highest ratio). All other grades fall between these.

reference_rules.rule: EEO category 1.1 is reserved exclusively for grades 9 (VP) and 10 (C-Suite). Grade 5 (Lead) and grades 1–2 have no EEO category assigned in visible seed data, implying EEO reporting covers only grades 3–4 (2.0), 6–8 (1.2), and 9–10 (1.1).
reference_rules.evidence: JOB_TITLES with EEO_CATEGORY='1.1': GRADE_ID IN (9,10). EEO_CATEGORY='1.2': GRADE_ID IN (6,8). EEO_CATEGORY='2.0': GRADE_ID IN (3,4). No EEO_CATEGORY on GRADE_ID IN (1,2,5).

reference_rules.rule: Managers skip Grade 7 (Senior Manager) entirely in the seed job title catalogue — there are Manager titles at Grade 6 and Director titles at Grade 8, but no titles defined for Grade 7. Promotions from Manager to Director therefore skip a grade level.
reference_rules.evidence: JOB_TITLES rows: GRADE_ID=6 (MGR-DEV, MGR-OPS, MGR-PAY, MGR-SALES), GRADE_ID=8 (DIR-IT, DIR-HR), zero rows with GRADE_ID=7.

reference_rules.rule: There is no VP defined for Sales, Operations, Legal, or Marketing in the JOB_TITLES seed, despite those departments existing. Only VP-HR (JOB_ID=10), VP-FIN (11), and VP-SALES (12) are seeded — implying a VP layer exists only for HR, Finance, and Sales.
reference_rules.evidence: VP-level titles (GRADE_ID=9): JOB_ID=10 (VP-HR), JOB_ID=11 (VP-FIN), JOB_ID=12 (VP-SALES). No VP-IT, VP-OPS, VP-LEGAL, VP-MKT defined.

reference_rules.rule: JOB_ID numbering is tiered by organizational level in blocks of 10: IDs 1–9 = C-Suite, 10–19 = VP, 20–29 = Director, 30–39 = Manager, 40–49 = Senior IC, 50–59 = Mid-level IC, 60–69 = Junior/Entry IC (implied by truncated data). This means any validation of job level can use range checks on JOB_ID.
reference_rules.evidence: JOB_ID=1–3 (C-Suite Grade 10); JOB_ID=10–12 (VP Grade 9); JOB_ID=20–21 (Director Grade 8); JOB_ID=30–33 (Manager Grade 6); JOB_ID=40–43 (Senior Grade 4); JOB_ID=50–53 (Mid-level Grade 3); employees reference JOB_ID=61,62 in grade 1–2 range.

reference_rules.rule: DEPT_ID is numbered in multiples of 10 for top-level departments (1, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70) and in consecutive integers for sub-departments (IT=30 → ITDEV=31, ITOPS=32). This encoding means a sub-department's DEPT_ID is always within 9 of its parent's DEPT_ID.
reference_rules.evidence: DEPT_ID=1 (EXEC, parent=NULL), DEPT_ID=10 (HR, parent=1), DEPT_ID=20 (FIN, parent=1), DEPT_ID=30 (IT, parent=1), DEPT_ID=31 (ITDEV, parent=30), DEPT_ID=32 (ITOPS, parent=30), DEPT_ID=40 (SALES, parent=1)...

reference_rules.rule: Cost center codes follow a strict hierarchy-encoded convention: CC-{n}000 for top-level (CC-1000=EXEC), CC-{n}{d}00 for second-level (CC-1100=HR, CC-1200=FIN), and CC-{n}{d}{s}0 for third-level sub-departments (CC-1310=ITDEV, CC-1320=ITOPS). This makes cost center codes parseable for hierarchy without a database join.
reference_rules.evidence: CC-1000 (EXEC), CC-1100 (HR), CC-1200 (FIN), CC-1300 (IT), CC-1310 (ITDEV), CC-1320 (ITOPS), CC-1400 (SALES), CC-1500 (MKT), CC-1600 (OPS), CC-1700 (LEGAL)

reference_rules.rule: There is exactly one organizational root: EXEC (DEPT_ID=1) is the only department with PARENT_DEPT_ID=NULL. All other departments have a non-null parent, enforcing a single-root tree hierarchy.
reference_rules.evidence: Only DEPT_ID=1 has PARENT_DEPT_ID=NULL. All other 9 DEPARTMENTS rows have PARENT_DEPT_ID = 1 or 30.

reference_rules.rule: IT is the only department with sub-departments in the seed data. No other function (HR, Finance, Sales, etc.) has children. IT has exactly two children: ITDEV and ITOPS — a maximum depth of 2 in the visible hierarchy.
reference_rules.evidence: PARENT_DEPT_ID=30 appears on DEPT_ID=31 and DEPT_ID=32. No other DEPT_ID appears as a PARENT_DEPT_ID except DEPT_ID=1 and DEPT_ID=30.

reference_rules.rule: Geographic assignment is deterministic by function: HQ (New York) hosts Executive, HR, Finance, and Legal. CHI (Chicago) hosts IT (all sub-departments) and Operations. SF (San Francisco) hosts Sales and Marketing. No department spans multiple locations in seed data.
reference_rules.evidence: DEPT_CODE IN (EXEC, HR, FIN, LEGAL) → LOCATION_CODE='HQ'; DEPT_CODE IN (IT, ITDEV, ITOPS, OPS) → LOCATION_CODE='CHI'; DEPT_CODE IN (SALES, MKT) → LOCATION_CODE='SF'

reference_rules.rule: All DEPARTMENTS rows have MANAGER_EMP_ID=NULL in the reference-data seed. This is a deliberate chicken-and-egg deferral: department managers are assigned by UPDATE statements after employees are loaded (script 02+). Any application logic must tolerate NULL manager on departments.
reference_rules.evidence: All 10 DEPARTMENTS INSERT statements set MANAGER_EMP_ID=NULL explicitly.

reference_rules.rule: The CEO (EMP_ID=1) is the sole employee with MANAGER_EMP_ID=NULL, establishing the top of the employee reporting chain. All other visible employees have a non-null MANAGER_EMP_ID.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=1 (JAMES RICHARDSON, JOB_ID=1 CEO): MANAGER_EMP_ID=NULL. All other EMPLOYEES rows have a non-null MANAGER_EMP_ID.

reference_rules.rule: Employee numbers are formatted as 'EMP-' followed by a zero-padded 6-digit sequential integer. The format encodes a system capacity of up to 999,999 employees before overflow.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_NUMBER values: 'EMP-000001', 'EMP-000002', 'EMP-000003', 'EMP-000010', 'EMP-000011' ... (6-digit zero-padded)

reference_rules.rule: EMP_NUMBER gaps in the seed data (e.g. EMP-000004 through EMP-000009 are absent) imply EMP_NUMBER is assigned based on EMP_ID directly, not from a separate sequence. Gaps in EMP_ID cause gaps in EMP_NUMBER.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=1→EMP-000001, EMP_ID=2→EMP-000002, EMP_ID=3→EMP-000003, then next is EMP_ID=10→EMP-000010 (IDs 4–9 skipped, matching DEPT_ID-aligned ID assignment pattern).

reference_rules.rule: EMP_ID values are assigned to match DEPT_ID ranges, not from a single global sequence: Executive employees use IDs 1–3, HR employees use IDs 10–12, Finance employees use IDs 20–24, IT employees use IDs 30–37. This ties employee identity to department at creation time.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=1,2,3 in DEPT_ID 1,20,30 (Exec/CFO/CIO); EMP_ID=10,11,12 in DEPT_ID=10 (HR); EMP_ID=20–24 in DEPT_ID=20 (Finance); EMP_ID=30–37 in DEPT_ID=30–31 (IT)

reference_rules.rule: All 25 seeded employees have EMPLOYMENT_TYPE='FULL_TIME' and EMPLOYMENT_STATUS='ACTIVE'. No seed rows for contractors, part-time, on-leave, terminated, or probationary employees — the system baseline assumes a fully active permanent workforce.
reference_rules.evidence: EMPLOYMENT_TYPE='FULL_TIME' and EMPLOYMENT_STATUS='ACTIVE' on all visible INSERT INTO EMPLOYEES statements.

reference_rules.rule: All dates are inserted using TO_DATE with format mask 'YYYY-MM-DD', enforcing ISO date format as the canonical input format for all date columns (HIRE_DATE, DATE_OF_BIRTH). CREATED_DATE uses SYSDATE (server time).
reference_rules.evidence: HIRE_DATE=TO_DATE('2010-03-15','YYYY-MM-DD'), DATE_OF_BIRTH=TO_DATE('1968-07-22','YYYY-MM-DD'), CREATED_DATE=SYSDATE on all rows.

reference_rules.rule: Seed hire dates span 2010-03-15 (CEO) to 2022-06-15 (Finance junior), a 12-year window. No employee was hired before 2010, establishing 2010 as the implied system go-live or data migration cutoff date.
reference_rules.evidence: Earliest HIRE_DATE: TO_DATE('2010-03-15','YYYY-MM-DD') for EMP_ID=1. Latest visible: TO_DATE('2022-06-15','YYYY-MM-DD') for EMP_ID=24.

reference_rules.rule: Seed dates of birth range from 1968-07-22 (CEO, ~57 at 2026) to 1997-10-30 (EMP_ID=24 Andrew Patel, ~28 at 2026). This implies the system supports employees aged approximately 25–60, with no under-18 or over-65 employees in baseline data.
reference_rules.evidence: Earliest DATE_OF_BIRTH: TO_DATE('1968-07-22','YYYY-MM-DD') for EMP_ID=1. Latest: TO_DATE('1997-10-30','YYYY-MM-DD') for EMP_ID=24.

reference_rules.rule: Employee location always matches the department's assigned location — no employee in the seed data is assigned to a location that differs from their department's location_code. Cross-location assignments are not represented.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=1 DEPT_ID=1 (EXEC→HQ) LOCATION_CODE='HQ'; EMP_ID=3 DEPT_ID=30 (IT→CHI) LOCATION_CODE='CHI'; EMP_ID=32 DEPT_ID=31 (ITDEV→CHI) LOCATION_CODE='CHI'.

reference_rules.rule: JOB_ID values 61 and 62 are referenced in employee data but are absent from the visible JOB_TITLES seed (which was truncated after JOB_ID=53). Based on the ID-range pattern (60–69 = junior/entry-level ICs) and the context of the employees assigned (Emily Johnson hired 2019 in HR dept, Andrew Patel hired 2022 in Finance dept), these are entry-level or junior roles in the Grade 1–2 range.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=12 EMILY JOHNSON DEPT_ID=10 (HR) JOB_ID=61 hired 2019-01-07; EMP_ID=24 ANDREW PATEL DEPT_ID=20 (Finance) JOB_ID=62 hired 2022-06-15. JOB_TITLES seed is truncated mid-insert after JOB_ID=53.

reference_rules.rule: ACTIVE_FLAG uses single-character string values ('Y'/'N'), not numeric booleans (1/0) or Oracle CHAR(1) boolean conventions. All seed records are 'Y'; 'N' is implied for logical deletes. This is a soft-delete pattern — records are never physically deleted.
reference_rules.evidence: ACTIVE_FLAG='Y' on all INSERT statements across both files. Column type and value consistent with VARCHAR2(1) soft-delete convention.

reference_rules.rule: All seed data is attributed to 'SYSTEM' as CREATED_BY, establishing that reference data is system-owned and not user-editable in a self-service workflow. Application logic should prevent non-SYSTEM users from modifying rows where CREATED_BY='SYSTEM'.
reference_rules.evidence: CREATED_BY='SYSTEM' on every INSERT statement in both seed files.

reference_rules.rule: The organisation is US-only at baseline: all three locations are in the United States with COUNTRY_CODE='US'. There is no multi-currency, multi-national, or tax-jurisdiction seed data, implying the initial system design targets a single-country payroll.
reference_rules.evidence: COUNTRY_CODE='US' on all three LOCATIONS rows (HQ, CHI, SF). No non-US country code appears anywhere in either seed file.

reference_rules.rule: Phone number format follows the North American Numbering Plan (NNN-NNN-NNNN). Location phones encode the area code of their city: HQ uses 212 (New York), CHI uses 312 (Chicago), SF uses 415 (San Francisco). Work phones of employees follow the same area code as their assigned location.
reference_rules.evidence: LOCATIONS: HQ PHONE='212-555-1000', CHI PHONE='312-555-2000', SF PHONE='415-555-3000'. EMP_ID=1 (HQ) PHONE_WORK='212-555-1001'; EMP_ID=3 (CHI) PHONE_WORK='312-555-2001'.

reference_rules.rule: Work phone numbers for employees are sequential extensions off the location base number. HQ employee extensions start at 212-555-1001 (CEO), then 1002 (CFO), 1003 (CIO), then 1101 for HR dept, 1201 for Finance, etc. The extension encodes both location and department.
Email addresses follow the pattern firstname.lastname@company.com (all lowercase), establishing a deterministic email generation rule. No domain variation by location, department, or employment type.
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=1: EMAIL='james.richardson@company.com'; EMP_ID=2: EMAIL='sarah.chen@company.com'; EMP_ID=36: EMAIL='priya.sharma@company.com'

reference_rules.rule: All employee names are stored in ALL CAPS (FIRST_NAME, LAST_NAME). This is a data entry convention or an application-enforced UPPER() constraint, not a display convention — application code must apply INITCAP() or title-case formatting for display.
reference_rules.evidence: FIRST_NAME='JAMES', LAST_NAME='RICHARDSON'; FIRST_NAME='SARAH', LAST_NAME='CHEN'; FIRST_NAME='PRIYA', LAST_NAME='SHARMA' — consistently uppercase across all rows.

reference_rules.rule: The reporting chain in the seed data reflects a strict hierarchy where each employee's MANAGER_EMP_ID is always a more senior employee in the same or parent department. Cross-department reporting is used only at the C-Suite level (CFO and CIO report to CEO across department boundaries).
reference_rules.evidence: EMP_ID=2 (CFO, FIN dept) MANAGER_EMP_ID=1 (CEO, EXEC dept); EMP_ID=3 (CIO, IT dept) MANAGER_EMP_ID=1 (CEO, EXEC dept). All other employees report to managers within or one level above their department.
